item.title: Vance appears to soften U.S. demands on Iranian nuclear enrichment
item.description: Vance says Iran must do "something meaningful on enrichment capacity" to end the war, as Rubio claims Tehran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Isaias becomes first hurricane of 2026 Atlantic season, threatens Gulf Coast
item.description: Hurricane Isaias developed late Wednesday as the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, taking aim at the Gulf Coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: Democrats invest more heavily in Gina Hinojosa as Pritzker offers support
item.description: Last week, more than 70 Latino Democratic leaders sent a letter to Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, the chair of the DGA, urging the group to invest $10 million to help Hinojosa's campaign.

item.title: Man eyed Mall of America for attack, pledged allegiance to ISIS, FBI says
item.description: An 18-year-old Twin Cities man accused of telling an FBI informant he planned to carry out an attack later this month at Mall of America was arrested at gunpoint Tuesday in Richfield, Minnesota, during an arranged meeting to buy an assault rifle, according to a federal criminal complaint filed Wednesday.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend
item.description: Tropical Storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf and is expected to become a hurricane by Thursday before approaching the U.S. northern Gulf Coast on Friday, according to forecasters.

item.title: 3 years on, survivors and family members of victims recall Oct. 7 massacre
item.description: Survivors of the Oct. 7 terrorist attack by Hamas in Israel spoke with CBS News to recount the harrowing day. Family members of those who did not survive remember them and their legacies.

item.title: Obama hosts fundraiser with Senate Democrats weeks before midterms
item.description: Former President Barack Obama headlined a fundraiser for the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Wednesday night to discuss the stakes of the upcoming midterm election.

item.title: Newly obtained footage shows Iran attack on major U.S. post in Kuwait
item.description: CBS News obtained new video from a person on the ground showing an Iranian attack on a U.S. base at the beginning of the war.

item.title: Russia open to a Trump-Putin call as questions mount over plague lab death
item.description: Russia says it's open to a Trump-Putin phone call as concern and questions mount over a woman's death of "pneumonia of unknown origin."

item.title: Texas executes man after lawyers sought to stop procedure, citing Christa Pike
item.description: Jamaal Howard was executed by lethal injection after his lawyers tried to argue that he faced risks similar to Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's attempt to put her to death.

item.title: Protesters ejected from raucous Trump rally in Texas
item.description: Several hecklers were removed from President Trump's rally in Texas late Wednesday, drawing jeers from the crowd as the president made fun of the protesters.

item.title: 1 dead, 3 missing after boat sinks near Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay
item.description: One person died and three were missing in San Francisco Bay on Tuesday after a boat with 20 people on board sank near Alcatraz Island, authorities said.

item.title: Alleged Chinese agent to remain in custody, judge rules, amid flight-risk fears
item.description: California realtor Wanying Zhang is facing federal prosecution for allegedly surveilling the Taiwanese president's son in Washington last year at the direction of Chinese government officials.

item.title: Apple reportedly developing home AI security device that won't record video
item.description: Apple is reportedly developing a home security system that will use AI to track movement without recording video footage. CNET senior technology reporter Abrar Al-Heeti joins CBS News.

item.title: Trump stumps for Paxton in Texas ahead of midterms
item.description: The midterms are heating up, with President Trump in Texas for the third time in less than a month to campaign for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. CBS News congressional correspondent Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Mamdani criticized for statement mourning Oct. 7 and condemning Israel
item.description: A statement by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani that recognized three years since Hamas' "horrific" attack on Israel — and criticized Israel's "ongoing genocide" in Gaza — has drawn fury from some Democrats.

item.title: Oct. 7 survivor shares her story and advocates to stop antisemitism, extremism
item.description: Three years after Hamas' terrorist attacks against Israel on Oct. 3, 2023, Natalie Sanandaj, a Nova festival attack survivor and public affairs officer at the Combat Antisemitism Movement, joins CBS News with her story about that day.

item.title: Cornell rape probe reignites debate on sexual assault prevention on college campuses
item.description: The Cornell rape investigation is sparking discussions on what needs to be done to prevent sexual assault on college campuses. Hanna Stotland, an independent admissions consultant who previously advised one of the men named in Jane Doe's lawsuit, joins CBS News.

item.title: 13-year-old carves 500-pound monster pumpkin, planted with seeds from his grandmother
item.description: When a 13-year-old got the gift of pumpkin seeds from his grandmother, he chose not to toss them aside, but to plant them and be patient. With the help of a forklift, a saw, and a chisel, he carved the 500-pound monster and its little 300-pound sibling. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Inside the hourslong search for missing boy in Maryland: "I got him!"
item.description: Police found a little boy just feet from a busy road, with the help of a bloodhound named Bo. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Looking back 3 years after Oct. 7, 2023: "There was the constant fear"
item.description: Wednesday marks three years since Hamas terrorists killed more than 1,200 Israelis, including dozens of Americans, and took 250 people hostage. Holly Williams reports from Tel Aviv.

item.title: Christa Pike has pneumonia, unable to move arms after botched execution
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, the Tennessee inmate who survived two doses of a lethal injection during her botched execution last week, shared an update on her health condition.

item.title: Exclusive videos show Iranian drone strike on U.S. base in Kuwait
item.description: Video shows an Iranian drone strike on a U.S. military installation in Kuwait, one of at least eight different countries to face Iranian fire in this war, which has damaged or destroyed billions in U.S. military property. Jonah Kaplan has the exclusive.

item.title: What Christa Pike asked when she woke up from failed execution
item.description: Christa Pike's attorneys accuse Tennessee prison officials of delaying access to their client for over two hours after she regained consciousness on Tuesday following a failed execution attempt. Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: 10/7: CBS Evening News
item.description: Tropical storm intensifies off Gulf Coast; FBI foils ISIS-inspired plot in Minnesota.

item.title: Sen. Thom Tillis says Hegseth is "just out of his depth"
item.description: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina was under intense pressure to confirm Pete Hegseth as defense secretary, and after wavering, he ultimately voted yes. In his new book "How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents," Tillis says that decision hasn't aged well. Tillis joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Maduro expected to face new charges of torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons
item.description: An attorney for Maduro told CBS News that he has not been given notice that additional charges could be coming.

item.title: 10/7: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump returns to Texas to stump for Paxton in San Antonio; new videos show Iranian attacks on U.S. military base in Kuwait.

item.title: Trump pitches Trump International Golf Course for site of "presidential retreat"
item.description: It's not yet clear what the taxpayer benefit would be for such a build, or how much it would cost.

item.title: Shock gloves bought by ICE cause intense pain, Army study says
item.description: Participants in a military exercise felt intense pain, stopped fighting immediately and feared additional exposures, according to an Army study.
